cards.text: Job, a man from the land of Uz, has lost his children, his animals and his health, and three friends came to comfort him (Job 1-2). Then Job cursed the day he was born (Job 3:1). Now one of those friends, Eliphaz the Temanite, finally speaks.

Eliphaz asks if Job will be wearied if someone ventures a word, then says, "Yet who can keep from speaking?" Friend, that's the old "Can I be honest with you?" and NOBODY in history has ever waited for the answer to that one.

cards.question: Eliphaz starts with a compliment. He says Job used to strengthen feeble hands, and his words would ___ people who stumbled.

cards.text: Then comes the "But now": trouble has come upon Job, Eliphaz says, and he's weary and dismayed. Friend, a compliment with a "but" right behind it isn't a compliment, it's a RUNWAY.

cards.question: True or false: Eliphaz asks Job whether his reverence should be his confidence, and the uprightness of his ways his hope.
Eliphaz pleads with Job to consider one question. What's it about?

cards.text: Hold that question for a second, friend. Back at the start, God Himself said there's no one on earth like Job, a man who is blameless and upright, who fears God and shuns evil (Job 1:8).

cards.question: Eliphaz says he's seen it for himself: those who plow iniquity and sow trouble ___ the same.
Eliphaz says the people who sow trouble perish and are consumed. What does he say they perish by?

cards.text: Then Eliphaz goes full nature documentary. Out come the lions, roaring and growling.

cards.question: True or false: in Eliphaz's picture, the roaring lions end up strong and well fed.

cards.text: Then Eliphaz gets spooky. A word came to him secretly, he says, a whisper in disquieting visions in the night, when deep sleep falls on men.

cards.question: During those disquieting night visions, Eliphaz says ___ and trembling came over him and made all his bones shudder.

cards.text: Then a spirit glided past his face, and the hair on his body bristled. Baker, I don't even HAVE body hair, but if a spirit glided past my face, this mustache would pack a bag and leave WITHOUT me.

cards.question: True or false: when the spirit stood still, Eliphaz could clearly make out what it looked like.
A form looms before Eliphaz, and he hears a whispering voice. What does the voice ask?

answers.text: If a mortal can be more righteous than God
If a mortal can see God and still live
If a mortal can count all the stars

cards.question: The voice says God puts no trust in His servants and charges His angels with error. So what does it say about people?

cards.text: People live in houses of clay with foundations in the dust, the voice says, and they can be crushed like a moth. Humbling, friend, but I can't argue: I once lost a stretching contest to a rubber band in that junk drawer.

cards.question: The voice says people are smashed to pieces from dawn to dusk. True or false: it says they perish with everyone noticing.

cards.text: The voice ends with a picture: tent cords pulled up, so they die without wisdom. That's the end of the whisper, but Eliphaz is just warming UP.
Eliphaz keeps going. Call out if you please, he tells Job, but who will answer, and to which of the holy ones will you turn?

cards.question: Eliphaz names two things he says can kill a fool and slay the simple. What are they?

cards.text: Eliphaz says he's seen a fool taking root. Settling in, getting comfy, unpacking the boxes, and then SUDDENLY his house was cursed.

cards.question: True or false: Eliphaz says the fool's sons have a defender when they're crushed in court.
What does Eliphaz say happens to the cursed fool's harvest?
Eliphaz turns to where trouble comes from. True or false: he says distress springs up out of the dust.

cards.text: Then Eliphaz says, "Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward." Friend, I started out in a clearance bin at a bakery that was closing, so born to trouble? I was born ON SALE.
Then Eliphaz gets personal. He tells Job what he'd do if he were in Job's place.

cards.question: If Eliphaz were in Job's place, what does he say he would do?

answers.text: Take his case to the elders

cards.text: Eliphaz describes God as the One who does great and unsearchable things, wonders without number. He gives rain to the earth and sends water upon the fields.

cards.question: Eliphaz says God sets the ___ on high, so mourners are lifted to safety.

cards.text: God thwarts the crafty, Eliphaz says, so they grope at noon like it's night, but He saves the needy from the powerful. So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.

cards.question: Eliphaz tells Job not to despise the discipline of the Almighty. He says the man whom God ___ is blessed indeed.
True or false: Eliphaz says the God who wounds and strikes also binds and heals.

cards.text: Then Eliphaz tells Job what God will do for him: rescue him from six calamities, and in seven no harm will touch him. In famine He'll redeem him from death, and in battle from the stroke of the sword.

cards.question: Eliphaz says Job will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue. What does he say Job will do at destruction and famine?

cards.text: Eliphaz says Job will have a covenant with the stones of the field, the wild animals at peace with him and his tent secure. Peace with the STONES, friend, and I couldn't even keep the peace between two dead batteries in that junk drawer.

cards.question: True or false: Eliphaz tells Job his offspring will be few.
Eliphaz says Job will come to the grave like a sheaf of grain gathered in season. How will he come?

cards.text: Eliphaz wraps up: "Indeed, we have investigated, and it is true! So hear it and know for yourself." That's his whole speech, friend, but trust me, this story is a LONG way from done.
